findings_addressed: R-20-H7 — the gate EXISTS and is GREEN. scripts/check-c1-conformance.sh exits 0 on the tree at head; all 26 CHECKABLE clauses of the ratified OPP-12 C-1 converged contract hold against as-built code.

The gate is pinned to the AMENDED contract (efa8d584). The un-amended Q6(b) mandated an anonymous surrogate that the ratified TC-11 pin A forbids ever implementing; a registry derived from that text would have been permanently red and would have held the breaking-pair publish forever. Both the gate header and the pin's _comment record this as the reason the contract's bytes are pinned at all.
Dual-homed per the settled design: preflight.sh --landing §10 (PREVENT) and an always-on ci.yml job (DETECT), both invoking THE SAME script so the predicate cannot diverge.

Recurrence guard: scripts/tests/test_check_c1_conformance.sh, 126 assertions across 17 arms (17 after the fix-1 round added seven sub-arms 12d-12j to the existing arm-12 section), every failure arm driven by a purpose-built divergent fixture.

FIX-1 / codex §9 round 1, finding #1 [P2] — CLOSED. The readiness vocabulary was BLACKLISTED, not pinned: 'EXACTLY {ready, embedding}' was probed as two `present` probes plus one `absent DenseReadiness::Pending`. codex demonstrated `pub enum DenseReadiness { Ready, Embedding, Failed }` clearing the gate with exit 0. Now closed by CONSTRUCTION with two new structural probe kinds — enum_exact (parses the enum body, compares variant SET *and* COUNT) and arms_exact (parses `impl Ty { fn f }`, compares the (variant, string) match-arm pairs as a LIST so a duplicate spelling is visible). A third variant fails whatever it is called; a third accepted STRING spelling fails even with the enum untouched.

FIX-1 / codex §9 round 1, finding #2 [P2] — CLOSED. The NO-DATA-MIGRATION `absent` regexes were case-sensitive and single-space-anchored; codex cleared the gate with `insert into canonical_attributes select * from old;`. New helper insert_into(table) emits (?i) plus all five SQLite conflict clauses (ABORT/FAIL/IGNORE/REPLACE/ROLLBACK) plus \s+ between every token (newlines included) plus an optionally quoted/bracketed table name. SCOPE was re-read and is now written into the gate header: the clause forbids a MIGRATION/BACKFILL of PRE-EXISTING rows, the probes stay scoped to the SCHEMA crate (which IS the migration ladder), and the LEGITIMATE same-transaction projection INSERTs live in the ENGINE (configure_projections, lib.rs ~16663/16669) and are out of scope — so widening to case-insensitive cannot false-positive on them. The one residual is stated plainly in the header rather than hidden: a doc comment literally spelling `insert into canonical_attributes` in the schema crate would trip it, which is a false RED (the safe side) rather than the false GREEN it replaces.

FIX-1 SWEEP — both DEFECT CLASSES were searched for across every other clause assertion, and THREE MORE INSTANCES were found and fixed in the same round. Open-vocabulary probes: C1-Q6A-THREE-ROLES ('exactly {filterable, rankable, searchable}') had a blacklist of two names, so a fourth role under any other name passed; C1-Q6B-IDSPACE-TOTAL-THREE ('total over exactly those three') had FOUR `present` probes and NO negative probe at all, so a fourth variant — the precise violation of totality — could not be detected even in principle. Case-sensitive SQL: C1-TE-CUSTOM-TOKENIZER-DEFERRED's `absent CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE property_search_index` over the ENGINE had the identical uppercase anchor. All three now have their own RED-first fixture arms (12f, 12g, 12j), each of which exited 0 before this round.

FIX-1 NON-INSTANCES, checked and deliberately left alone: the Rust IDENTIFIER negative probes (ProjectionRole::Vector, ProjectionRole::Fts, EntityTypeSpec, id_prefix, idPrefix, DenseReadiness::Pending, `pub id: Option<IdSpace>`) stay CASE-SENSITIVE because case is significant in Rust — folding case there would manufacture false positives, not close a hole. C1-Q4-NO-PROVISIONAL-CONCEPT was already (?i). C1-Q6B-ID-NON-NULL's `absent pub id: Option<IdSpace>` is a single-spelling blacklist, but its paired `present pub id: IdSpace,` probe carries the obligation on its own (a change to Option makes the present probe fail), so it is not an open vocabulary.

blockers_encountered.what: Wiring the gate into preflight §10 turned FOUR sibling suites red (test_preflight_landing, test_check_ledgers, test_check_board_currency, test_check_governed_surface_pin). Their throwaway fixture repos carry no C-1 contract, no pin and no sources, so the gate exited 2 and the anti-fail-open clause correctly refused to certify the tree.
blockers_encountered.how: The gate was NOT weakened. Followed the established repair (T1b for ledger-integrity, T1e for the governed-surface pin): a new seeder helper scripts/tests/lib/c1-conformance-fixture.sh, called from each fixture builder. No bypass, no env escape hatch, no --skip, no conditional that makes the gate inert.
blockers_encountered.deviation_recorded: The seeder COPIES the real artifacts, a deliberate departure from its synthetic sibling lib/governed-surface-fixture.sh. A synthetic C-1 pair is IMPOSSIBLE, not merely undesirable: the gate's implemented-assertion set is a constant inside the script and the registry bijection is rigid in both directions, so any pin not registering exactly the 26 CHECKABLE ids reports MALFORMED — the very failure the seeder exists to remove. The header states this and why the resulting coupling is acceptable (the C-1 pin, unlike the governed-surface pin, is not expected to trip during 0.8.20).

The pin carries sha256_whitespace_normalized in addition to sha256 + git_blob_sha1. It is used ONLY to tell the reader whether a divergence was formatting-only (the brief requires that message); it is never a substitute for the content hash.

residual_scope_statement.where: scripts/check-c1-conformance.sh header, section 'RESIDUAL SCOPE — READ BEFORE ROUND 3'; one-paragraph mirror in scripts/c1-conformance-pin.json's _comment.
residual_scope_statement.epistemic_status_claimed: This gate is a TRIPWIRE AGAINST DRIFT, not a proof of conformance. Threat model: a future contributor who changes as-built code without noticing that a ratified cross-repo contract said otherwise. NOT an adversarial control — it cannot stop someone deliberately smuggling a backfill past CI, and nothing assembled out of regexes over source text could.
classes_documented_as_uncatchable: 1. DYNAMICALLY COMPOSED SQL — format!("INSERT INTO {} ...", TABLE), push_str from fragments, a table name in a const/static. The gate reads `{}`, not the table.

2. ANOTHER ROUTE TO THE SAME TABLE — qualified() closes the SPELLINGS of the pinned NAME, not every ROUTE: an ATTACHed alias chosen at runtime, a VIEW or INSTEAD OF TRIGGER writing the table under a different name, ALTER TABLE ... RENAME.

3. IDENTIFIER INDIRECTION IN RUST — `const PENDING: &str = "pending";` defeats the string-literal check; macro_rules!/paste!-generated enum bodies and impl blocks are never expanded; concat_idents!-style construction defeats the EntityTypeSpec/id_prefix negative-space probes; a type alias or re-export defeats the identifier probes.

4. CONVERSION SURFACES OUTSIDE THE NAMED FUNCTION — arms_exact reads exactly `impl <Ty> { fn <fn> }`. An `impl FromStr for <Ty>`, a `From<&str>`, or a free `fn parse_readiness(&str) -> Option<DenseReadiness>` admits an extra spelling without touching the block the gate reads. This is the clearest proof the approach cannot be COMPLETED by widening: a free function is ordinary Rust and no impl-scoped check can reach it.
5. NORMALISING COMPARISONS — to_lowercase()/trim()/eq_ignore_ascii_case widen the accepted vocabulary WITHOUT introducing a new string literal.
6. CONDITIONAL COMPILATION — nothing models #[cfg(...)]; text under a disabled feature reads exactly like shipped code. (Errs RED, not green.)
7. BEHAVIOUR, and THE MEMEX REPO — already stated before this round: behavioural clauses assert only that the NAMED TEST still exists, and 12 clauses are CROSS-REPO by classification.
residual_scope_statement.error_bias_documented: Every ambiguity resolves toward RED: an unparseable enum body, an impl block the reader cannot find, an unreadable file and a missing tree are all failures (exit 1 / exit 2), never skips; and the text-scoped probes WILL trip on a doc comment or an error message that spells the forbidden thing. Noisy false positives with false negatives confined to the documented list is the correct bias for a gate that HOLDS A PUBLISH.
residual_scope_statement.why_this_stopping_point: The threat model is accidental drift by a future contributor, not a malicious actor. Residual class 4 is the decisive argument that no amount of further widening reaches soundness — a free conversion function is ordinary Rust and lies outside any impl-scoped check — so the marginal return on a third regex round is ~0 while the same-finding budget is finite. Making the boundary EXPLICIT converts an open-ended asymptote into a reviewable scope decision.
residual_scope_statement.consequence_for_reviewers: Stated in the header: a finding that the gate misses something ON the documented list is TRUE and is NOT a defect in the patch — the answer to it is a different mechanism, not another regex. A finding that it misses a spelling of a PINNED NAME in LITERAL source text IS a real defect.

tc37_semantics_change.question: Once a probe's subject is a TREE rather than a FILE, what does 'missing' mean?
tc37_semantics_change.decision: TWO ways a tree fails to be a subject, both exit 2 (TC-37 evaporation path #4, whose header text was amended to say so). (a) THE DIRECTORY IS ABSENT — unambiguous, and unchanged behaviour. (b) THE DIRECTORY YIELDS ZERO CANDIDATE FILES (empty, or nothing matching exts, or only binaries) — NEW this round, and the judgement call. Decided for exit 2: a NEGATIVE assertion that examined zero files is trivially satisfiable and would report 'no violation found' having looked at nothing. tc37_semantics_change.implementation_consequence: walk_tree() now returns a LIST rather than yielding, because 'examined nothing' is only knowable after the walk completes and a caller that returns on the first match would never let a generator get there. It is cached per (tree, exts).

(b) THE CRATE, AND THE INVOCATION. This gate reads source and manifest TEXT. It does not know whether the crate is still a workspace member, nor how CI actually invokes cargo (an `--exclude`, a filter argument, a job that stops running).
(c) `#[cfg]` INSIDE a body — an assertion compiled out while the test still runs and passes vacuously. Class #6 again.
